title: Merchant Harbor — Handshake plan & objection flows
content:
Quick context
- Merchant Harbor: mid-market payments/merchant acquisition platform (focus on SMB retail) — HQ SF, series B-ish per Crunchbase. Likely annual processing volume \u003e$200M.
- Eng/org signals: has internal ML team but lean infra; sensitive to vendor lock and latency for checkout experiences.
- Why we care: product fits (low-latency hosted inference for chat/automations, private deployment option for compliance), potential Dedicated deal if they want committed throughput for webhook-driven flows.

Account snapshot (fast bullets)
- Key contact: Aaron Chen (Head of Payments Integrations) — ex-Stripe, based in SF.
- Procurement: Sarah Ng (Dir of Vendor Ops) — procurement + legal gate.
- Tech lead: Viktor M. (principal eng) — cares about token costs and runtime determinism.
- Org priority next 6 months: reduce checkout latency, automate merchant onboarding, pilot conversational merchant support.

Primary hypothesis / value props to surface
- Consistent sub-100ms token-level tail latency for short prompts (checkout prompts) on Dedicated -> reduces checkout friction.
- Predictable unit economics via batching/caching/Optimize recommendations -> helps keep per-merchant margins.
- Private deployment option + KMS/HSM integration for high-security merchants -> avoids data residency hangups.

Outbound play / suggested sequence (2-week cadence)
1) Email 1 (intro — value signal) 
   - Short subject: "Merchant Harbor + predictable checkout AI latency"
   - Body bullets: 1–2 sentences on who we are, 1 measurable claim (e.g., "we’ve helped X teams cut tail token latency by 60% at scale"), ask for 20-min discovery.
2) LinkedIn connect + 1-line note to Aaron referencing a specific Merchant Harbor blog post (shows research).
3) Email 2 (customer story + ask) after 4 business days — include one-pager for pilot (see pilot outline below).
4) Voicemail + calendar poll if no response on email 2.

Short email templates (skeletal)
- Cold opener: "Aaron — quick note from Redwood Inference. We help payments teams keep AI-driven checkout flows under 100ms tail latency while cutting per-token spend 30% via batching + caching. Curious if you’re open to a short chat about potential pilot?"
- Follow-up: "Sharing a 2-week pilot outline we did with a PSP — low lift, measurable latency and cost goals. If that sounds useful, happy to share more and sync."

Call / discovery cheat-sheet (for initial 20 minutes)
- Opening: confirm role + current priorities ("are checkout latency or merchant onboarding automation current top-3?")
- Tech checks: model types (RAG? LLM?), peak tokens/second, current p95/p99 latencies, current infra (self-hosted vs vendor), security controls required.
- Business checks: metrics they care about (conversion uplift, support deflection, onboarding time), budget windows, procurement timeline.
- Demo ask: offer 15-min focused demo of latency/observability (not feature-dump).

Objection flows (concise script)
- "We host everything in-house / vendor lock concerns" -> acknowledge, highlight Private deployment option + data plane controls, show examples of existing private customers and KMS/HSM support, propose a low-risk pilot with strict data deletion SLAs.
- "Price is too high" -> reframe as cost-per-conversion or cost-per-checkout; call out Optimize levers (auto-batching, KV caching) that reduce per-token spend and show sample math for their volume bucket. Offer short trial credits and committed pricing window tied to throughput.
- "Latency worries / unpredictable tail" -> share p95/p99 benchmarks (internal) and describe routing/fallback policies (can route to smaller model variant on overload). Offer a small synthetic load test and side-by-side comparison with their current baseline.
- "Legal / compliance slowdowns" -> offer list of docs we can fast-track (SOC2 summary, data flow diagram, sample DPA), suggest security sync with their legal/procurement + SRE.

Pilot outline (two-week technical pilot)
- Goal: demonstrate sub-100ms tail for targeted checkout prompts + 20–30% reduction in token costs for the same throughput.
- Scope: 1–2 endpoints, low-traffic merchant subset (1000 checkouts/day), metrics collection (latency histograms, cost by route).
- Deliverables: config + infra snapshot, dashboard access, weekly checkpoints, short writeup of findings and recommended rollout plan.
- Success criteria (mutually agreed): p99 latency \u003c= target, cost-per-checkout reduction >= X%, no data leakage issues.

Technical risks / notes to engineering stakeholder (Viktor)
- KV cache warm-up time for cold merchant population (need to discuss prefix caching strategy).
- Model variant compatibility with their RAG store (embedding dims, chunk size).
- Autoscale burst behavior when Black Friday-like events happen — need clear SLAs.

Open questions (internal)
- Who is the responsible legal contact at Merchant Harbor? (Sarah Ng confirm)
- Do they have a preferred cloud region for private deployments? (APAC expansion hints in press)
- Can we get a sample prompt + expected sequence length to estimate batch profiles?

Next steps (short checklist)
- [ ] Send Email 1 to Aaron + cc Marco for context (this week).
- [ ] Prep one-pager pilot doc (shared with Lina for review).
- [ ] Book a 30-min prep call with Viktor if they ask technical Qs; assign SRE lead.
- [ ] Gather SOC2 + DPA summary for procurement packet.

Notes to self / shorthand ideas
- Try to call out a concrete merchant use-case (POS autosuggest during checkout) in outreach — more concrete beats high-level claims.
- Keep pilot measurable and time-boxed; procurement likes clear exit criteria.
- Pricing negotiation lever: firm committed throughput vs. overage pricing tier.

Rough timeline idea
- Week 0: outreach (emails + LI).
- Week 1: discovery + technical intake.
- Week 2: pilot kickoff (2 weeks).
- Week 5: results + decision on Dedicated/reserved capacity or hosted + routing policy.

Scratch log (random notes)
- Found Aaron on Li: references Stripe migrations talk 2023 -> good convo opener.
- Crunchbase shows Series B 2022; implied runway comfortable but procurement still centralized.
- Connect Marco on thread once Aaron responds.

End of page
notes_summary: Outbound plan + discovery cheat sheet for Merchant Harbor; two-week pilot blueprint; objection handling scripts; internal next steps
